transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
Getting out of breath climbing the stairs.
Could you tell me a bit about when you first noticed getting out of breath on the stairs, how it came on, and whether you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?
It's crept up on me, maybe three months now.
How does this breathlessness affect your daily life, and what medicines are you taking at the moment, including any new or changed ones?
My memory's a bit poor. My wife does out my tablets.
Can you tell me about any other health problems you’ve had in the past, like illnesses that lasted a long time, operations, or times you were in hospital?
I've had atrial fibrillation five years. My late brother had it too.
Have you ever had an allergy or a bad reaction to a medicine, have you never had one, or are you not sure?
No, never had a reaction to anything.
When you get out of breath climbing the stairs, would you say it's mild and you can carry on, it's quite bad and makes you stop and rest, or are you not sure?
I have to stop halfway up. Fourteen stairs.
Can you describe what happens when you get out of breath on the stairs, where you feel it, and whether anything else happens at the same time?
It settles after a couple of minutes' rest.
Apart from needing to stop and catch your breath, is there anything else you notice while you're climbing the stairs or waiting for it to settle?
My ankles get puffy by the evening.
When you get out of breath on the stairs, where do you feel it most — in your chest, in your throat, or somewhere else, or are you not sure?
Just feel puffed out all over. My grandson's wedding is coming up.
What worries you most about how you've been feeling?
Worried about managing the stairs to bed.

You've mentioned your heart rhythm problem and that your brother had it too — is there anything else about your past health, like other ongoing health problems, past illnesses, operations, or hospital stays, that you'd like to add?
I had a heart attack twelve years back.
When you feel puffed out on the stairs, can you tell me what that feeling is like for you?
Just can't seem to catch my breath.
How, if at all, has getting out of breath on the stairs changed the things you do in a normal day?
I use two pillows now instead of one.
Is there anything else about your past health, such as other ongoing conditions, past illnesses, operations, or hospital stays, that you'd like to add?
Had a heart scan at hospital last year. Don't know the result.
Is there anything else you’d like to add?
No, that's about it, thank you.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
